# Find Subarrays With Equal Sum.

@example The neighbour sums are 1, 6, 7, -5 and 1: the first and the last are equal.
[2,-1,7,0,-5,6]
=> true

@example The neighbour sums 3, 4 and 6 all differ.
[5,-2,6,0]
=> false

@example Two numbers have a single neighbour sum, with nothing to match it.
[-6,-6]
=> false

# Three numbers: equal sums exactly when the first and last are equal.
# Here the only sum of 0 has no partner.
[4,-4,9]
=> false

[2,9,2]
=> true

# One of the equal sums is at index 0 (a map that uses 0 for "not seen"
# misses it).
[1,2,0,3]
=> true

# Two sums of 0.
[8,-8,8,1]
=> true

# Two equal negative sums.
[-7,-3,-4,-6]
=> true

# Equal sums of different numbers: 3 + 8 and 1 + 10.
[3,8,1,10]
=> true

# Values repeat, but the sums 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 don't.
[1,1,2,2,3,3]
=> false

# The extreme sums 2 * 10^9 and -2 * 10^9, repeated or not.
[1000000000,1000000000,1000000000]
=> true

[-1000000000,-1000000000,-1000000000]
=> true

[-1000000000,-1000000000,1000000000,1000000000]
=> false

# Large sums of both signs (a comparison by subtraction overflows): the
# sums at 1 and 5 are both -500000000.
[1000000000,500000000,-1000000000,-600000000,1000000000,400000000,-900000000,-999999999,999999999,900000000,-400000000,-1000000000]
=> true

[1000000000,600000000,-900000000,-1000000000,800000000,999999999]
=> false

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 2 small
[-999999999,500000000,500000000,1000000000,1000000000,1000000000]
=> true

@gen 3 small
[-9,-18,1,-22,17,4,27,28]
=> false

@gen 6 small
[3,3,1,1,1,-4,-1]
=> true

@gen 8 small
[-20,18,6,19,22,-15,-6,16]
=> false

@gen 9 small
[-2,0,1,-1,0,-3,3]
=> true

@gen 14 small
[1000000000,-999999999,999999999]
=> false

@gen 16 small
[-3,-1,-3]
=> true

@gen 17 small
[-22,18,15,-26,-29,-27,-23]
=> false
